summary: The cardholder starts a new billing cycle with no previous balance, makes purchases that push the account above the $1,000 credit limit, and reaches statement close while still over limit. The scenario is designed to probe over-limit behavior at statement close while also including the modeled minimum-payment and grace-period obligations in the timeline.
assumptions: The account begins a new billing cycle with no previous balance, so the grace-period condition is satisfied for new purchases under clause.6.grace_period.

The issuer allows the purchase transactions to post even though the total outstanding balance exceeds the credit limit; this scenario tests the contractual over-limit outcome at statement close rather than transaction denial behavior.
No payments are made before statement close, so the statement new balance remains above the credit limit.
A periodic statement is generated on the statement_close date and reflects the posted purchases in this cycle.

The minimum payment obligation under clause.5.minimum_payment_obligation is included by scheduling a due check after statement close; in this archetype the payment is intentionally left unmet to keep focus on the over-limit condition at statement close.

Although the contract text also contains a disclosure table stating over-the-credit-limit penalty fees may be none, this scenario follows the modeled IR clause for over-limit behavior and fee-trigger conditions.
